title: WHEN GOD SPEAKS IN THE NIGHT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "each of the two men—the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were being held in prison—had a dream the same night, and each dream had a meaning of its own." - Gen 40:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
On the very same night, both the cupbearer and the baker have dreams — and each dream carries its own hidden meaning. These were not ordinary, random dreams; God was quietly speaking, revealing to these two men something of what lay ahead. And He arranged it so that both dreamed on the same night, in the same prison, where Joseph was waiting to interpret them.

This small verse reminds us that God is always at work, even in the quiet and the dark, even in places that seem forgotten by the world. A prison cell in Egypt, two troubled foreigners, a night's sleep — and God was moving in the midst of it all, setting up a chain of events that would change the course of nations.

We may think God is distant or inactive when life feels stuck and ordinary. But the Lord never stops working. He is orchestrating details we cannot see, weaving together circumstances, people, and timing according to a plan far bigger than we know.

Nothing in your life is too small or too dark for God's attention. In the sleepless night, in the forgotten place, in the ordinary day, He is at work. Trust that the God who arranged two dreams on one night in a prison is arranging the details of your life too, with wisdom and purpose you will one day see.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God is at work even when life feels stuck or dark?
2. Where might God be quietly arranging details I cannot see?
3. How does God's constant activity encourage me today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You never stop working, even in the quiet and forgotten places. Help me to trust that You are arranging the details of my life with wisdom and purpose, even when I cannot see it. Amen.
